messages.author: 1ed7409e40e78732
messages.subject: suspicious df in DIF output
parts:
Dear Phil,
I have actually two questions related to degrees of freedom reported by DIF function. I am trying to assess DIF for bifactor model in 2 groups. I have estimated the model using multipleGroup function (with invariant slopes and intercepts) and subsequently used DIF function to evaluate invariance on general factor only. I found the number of degrees of freedom in the output a bit suspicious.

1) using scheme "drop", each item evaluated for DIF should have 1 df I think (as only factor loading of that item on general factor is free in both groups). However, I am getting 2 df as you can see from below.

slopeinvariance.ethnics3 <- DIF(smaz.ethnics3, c('a3'), scheme = "drop", items2test = 1:ncol(smaz.ethnics3@Data$data), seq_stat = "SABIC", Wald = FALSE, p.adjust = "none", max_run = Inf, plotdif = TRUE, type = "trace", verbose = TRUE)
slopeinvariance.ethnics3

$q03_1
       AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC    logLik     X2  df   p
1 33794.04 33810.66 33952.84 34235.51 -16808.02    NaN NaN NaN
2 33758.23 33775.63 33920.59 34209.62 -16788.11 39.815   2   0

$q08_2
       AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC    logLik     X2  df   p
1 33794.04 33810.66 33952.84 34235.51 -16808.02    NaN NaN NaN
2 33775.25 33792.65 33937.61 34226.64 -16796.62 22.794   2   0

$q13_3
       AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC    logLik     X2  df   p
1 33794.04 33810.66 33952.84 34235.51 -16808.02    NaN NaN NaN
2 33773.30 33790.71 33935.66 34224.69 -16795.65 24.741   2   0

$q16_4
       AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC    logLik     X2  df   p
1 33794.04 33810.66 33952.84 34235.51 -16808.02    NaN NaN NaN
2 33711.53 33728.93 33873.89 34162.92 -16764.76 86.515   2   0

etc....


2) For threshold invariance (have 3 category responses and thus 2 thresholds) and the "drop" scheme I am getting 1 df, but I think I should get 2 df, see below.

thresholdinvariance.ethnics3 <- DIF(smaz.ethnics3, c('d1','d2'), scheme = "drop", items2test = 1:20, seq_stat = "SABIC", Wald = FALSE, p.adjust = "none", max_run = Inf, plotdif = TRUE, type = "trace", verbose = TRUE) 
thresholdinvariance.ethnics3

$q03_1
       AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC    logLik     X2  df   p
1 33794.04 33810.66 33952.84 34235.51 -16808.02    NaN NaN NaN
2 33762.19 33779.20 33922.77 34208.62 -16791.10 33.851   1   0

$q08_2
       AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC    logLik   X2  df   p
1 33794.04 33810.66 33952.84 34235.51 -16808.02  NaN NaN NaN
2 33773.34 33790.35 33933.92 34219.77 -16796.67 22.7   1   0

$q13_3
       AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC    logLik     X2  df   p
1 33794.04 33810.66 33952.84 34235.51 -16808.02    NaN NaN NaN
2 33770.30 33787.31 33930.87 34216.73 -16795.15 25.745   1   0

$q16_4
       AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC    logLik     X2  df   p
1 33794.04 33810.66 33952.84 34235.51 -16808.02    NaN NaN NaN
2 33766.80 33783.81 33927.38 34213.24 -16793.40 29.237   1   0

etc....

Any clues? Maybe a bug in the DIF function? Any comments and suggestions are welcome and appreciated.

Many thanks,
Jan

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: suspicious df in DIF output
parts:
Hi Jan,

Thanks for the report, but I'm unsure what the exact error is. Bifactor models shouldn't be supported in DIF() since it isn't exactly clear how to account for latent mean/variance differences in the traits due to the dimensional reduction algorithm constraints (i.e., you can't actually free latent means, variances, or covariances for the specific factors....so DIF() should have thrown an error). Of course, one could set up constraints by passing specific models to the bfactor(..., model2 = ?) input and/or modify the starting values directly, but obviously all constraints would have to be specified manually.

Would it be possible to send something a little more reproducible? I've attached a short simulation syntax to help you get started. Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: 1ed7409e40e78732
messages.subject: Re: suspicious df in DIF output
parts:
Dear Phil,
thanks a lot for the code. Building on your simulated data, I attach mine code. I do not use bfactor() but multipleGroup() instead where you can specify the corresponding invariance constraints and then DIF() works fine. It actually now shows the right degrees of freedom. I just re-run DIF() on my data (I did not changed anything) and the function now reports the right degrees of freedom. Strange, but it works now. So the error was somewhere between the keyboard and the computer screen. Thanks again.

Regards,
Jan 

Many thanks
